posts.message: Sansui AU-555A owners, I need a sanity check. Finished my first full recap on one over the weekend (power supply, both amp boards, plus the big filter caps) and now there's a hum in both channels that was NOT there before. It's there with the volume all the way down and nothing plugged in, and it doesn't change when I turn the knob. Nothing's getting hot, no smell. Did I screw something up or do new caps need to break in? Where would you start?

Terrence, on your AU-555A: a hum that showed up right after the recap, with nothing plugged in and no change on the volume knob, is nearly always on the power supply or ground side, not the preamp. New caps don't need to break in. I'd check these in order:

1. The ground lug at the main filter caps. On a lot of Sansuis from this era the ground return lands on a lug under the cap bracket, and the old cans are part of what holds it tight. Once they're out, that lug can end up loose or grounding through paint. Take it apart, clean it to bare metal, add a star washer and snug it down.
2. Filter cap polarity and values. Go through every new electrolytic against the service manual, the big ones especially. A reversed or undersized filter cap gives you a buzzy 120 Hz hum and runs warm.
3. Whatever you change, bring it back up on a dim-bulb tester: a 60 to 100 W incandescent bulb in series with the mains. It should flash and settle to a faint glow. If it stays bright, switch off and look for a short or a reversed cap before you go any further.

If it turns out to be a smooth, low 60 Hz hum rather than a buzz, look at grounding and lead dress around the power transformer instead.

Update on my AU-555A hum, for anyone who searches this later: FIXED. Kofi called it, it was the ground lug under the filter cap bracket. Turns out the old cans were what kept that lug clamped, and once they came out the nut worked loose and the ground ended up running through the paint. Bare metal, star washer, tightened down, and now it's dead quiet. Next one goes up on a dim-bulb tester like Kofi said. Every one of you should have one on the bench.
Anyone know if Windy City is doing early-bird entry again this year? Thinking about driving over Saturday.
heard Lena Marsh is spinning at Windy City?? anyone vending?
VPD raised list prices again 😤 where's everyone buying dial lamps and belts?
Palmer Woods estate sale Saturday. 19340 Strathcona Dr. Opens 8:00. Marantz receiver stack, a Sansui amp, about 400 LPs. Pictures from the preview below.
Saturday pick-ups done. Ama shot six pieces today and every one of them looks better in her photos than it does on my bench. Pizza for the crew tonight.
Rollers tonight, 6:30 from Roosevelt Park. No-drop pace, about 25 miles, lights for the way back. Wind's out of the west so the return leg should feel nice for once.
First Monday Rollers of the season on the Trek. My legs are reporting a winter spent hunched over a bench. Thank you Luis for waiting at every light.

Starting something new on Wednesdays. Every week we'll share one habit from the bench that keeps old gear alive, no fluff. This week: if a receiver crackles when you turn a knob, that's usually dirty controls, not a dying amp. Work every pot and switch twenty or thirty times before you judge it. Follow along here or on Instagram under #BenchNotes.
Kwame helped Ama photograph a turntable today. His job was holding the reflector. He held it very, very seriously.

Bench Notes, week two. Anything we bring home from an estate sale meets the dim-bulb tester before it ever sees a wall outlet. A 60 W bulb wired in series limits the current, so if a filter cap or transformer is shorted, the bulb glows bright instead of something inside letting out smoke. Cheap to build, and it saves a lot of heartbreak.

Estate-sale ride through University District this morning. Panniers came home with a Sansui tuner, two boxes of tubes and a very heavy spool of speaker wire. The bike handled it. My back has questions.

Electrician came by this afternoon to quote a dedicated 20 amp circuit for the garage. Running a variac, a scope and a heat gun off one tired outlet was never a long-term plan. Efua says she'll believe it when the kitchen lights stop dimming.

Small detail, big difference. Plenty of receivers reach us with cold-white LEDs someone dropped into the dial. We put them back to warm incandescent, or an LED color-matched to the original. Your dial should look like 1976 at night, not a parking garage.

Bench Notes: after any recap, and before the speakers go back on, the meter goes on the speaker terminals. We want DC offset sitting in the low millivolts, and that reading goes on the bench report for the unit. If it's high, something is wrong and the receiver doesn't leave the bench.

Grandmont-Rosedale this morning. The lady running the sale had a Thorens in her late husband's den and wanted to know it was going to someone who'd keep it playing. I promised her a photo once it's spinning again. That's the part of this work nobody puts in a business plan.
Ride's on tonight. 6:30 from Roosevelt Park. Storms looked iffy this morning but radar is clear after 5. Bring a rear light, we'll be rolling in close to sunset.
good crowd tonight!! shoutout to Kofi for fixing my rear derailleur at Michigan and Trumbull with a multitool and pure stubbornness
Field Day at Greenlawn. Kwame took the sack race very seriously and finished third, which he has explained to me is "basically first." Sunscreen was applied. Some of it stayed on.
Efua sent me the video of our Kwame walking across the gym at his moving-up and I have watched it ten times. First grade! God is good.
Kwame moved up to first grade this morning. Walked across that gym like he was collecting a Grammy. Proud of you, little man.

If your speaker surrounds crumble when you press them gently, they need a refoam, simple as that. Foam from the 70s and 80s breaks down no matter how carefully it was stored. We don't do speaker work in-house, but we're glad to point you to a good speaker shop.
Kwame's last day of school today and he already has a summer list: bike, library, and "help Daddy fix the radios." ❤️
Refoam season apparently. Six pairs of woofers on my shelf this week. If your surrounds look like old bread, bring them in. Dearborn Heights, Mon to Sat.
Coffee at Astro with Sam this morning. He's just getting into fixing up receivers and asked more good questions in an hour than I asked my whole first year. Michigan Ave was already busy at 8:30.

Here's how a receiver leaves our shop. Knobs come off and get bagged, the unit goes into an inner box, then two inches of foam on every side inside an outer box. Ama photographs every piece before the tape goes on, so you and we both know exactly how it left Detroit.
Heads up: we're away from the shop starting today for the holiday weekend. Messages will still get answered, just slower, and pick-ups resume next week. Happy Fourth, Detroit.
Day two at Sleeping Bear. Kwame climbed the Dune Climb twice and made it to the fourth firework before he fell asleep. Kofi has not mentioned a capacitor once, which might be a record ❤️
Thank you Jesus for travelling mercies for my children on their camping trip. Efua sent pictures of Kwame on the big sand hill. My grandson is growing too fast.
Rollers took the long way out toward Belle Isle tonight. Detroit in July from a bike seat is hard to beat.
Finished a 2A3 single-ended build for a customer in Grosse Pointe. Point to point, cathode bias, and I did not wind my own transformers because I'm not crazy. Ferndale bench is officially too small.
Prairie St block party is THIS Saturday from 3 o'clock! Bring a dish, bring a chair. Gerald is on the grill again. We still need someone with a sound system, any volunteers?
Tasha, I can bring a receiver and a pair of speakers for Saturday and be set up by 2:30. Just need an outdoor outlet and somebody to keep the little ones away from the cords.

Turntable humming? Work through it in order: ground wire to the GND post on your amp, then swap the RCA cables, then try a different outlet. Most of the time it's the ground wire, and that takes thirty seconds to fix.
Prairie St block party tonight. Ran a 1970s Marantz and a pair of Advents off an extension cord for six hours and nothing caught fire. Kwame was asleep on Lorraine's porch swing by nine.
What a block party. Thank you to everyone who cooked, cleaned and carried tables. Special thanks to Kofi for the music, Earl and Doris danced to every Motown song he played.

Thirteen weeks of Bench Notes, cut down to one minute. The video is up on our Instagram and we'd love to know which tip deserves its own longer version. Tell us in the comments here, we read every one.

Rode up to Ferndale and Royal Oak for the sales this morning. Long way to haul a turntable in panniers but the Surly didn't complain. Stopped for coffee on Woodward on the way back and a guy asked if the dust cover was for sale.
That warm meter glow is half the reason people fall for vintage receivers. When a meter lamp burns out, we match the color as well as the voltage, so both meters glow the same.
Back in Grandmont-Rosedale this morning. Patricia beat me to the record room again. One of these Saturdays I'll get there before her.

Saturday finds: a stack of Blue Note reissues, Pyrex in Butterprint and a lamp I absolutely did not need. The receiver man from Bagley was out on his bike again. I'll beat him to the records every time 😉
Arden Park this morning. Those houses are something else. Came home with nothing but a box of service manuals, which honestly is sometimes the best find of the day.
Dropped the Transit Connect at Seven Mile Auto & Brake this morning. Ten years fixing cars and I still pay someone to do my brakes. Bench time is worth more than my knuckles now.

Fresh off the bench, a receiver's first power-up goes into a dummy load, never into speakers. Ours is a bank of 8 ohm resistors that can take whatever a fault throws at them. Your speakers deserve better than being our test subject.
Back to school tomorrow for both of us. Kwame's first grade backpack has been packed since Thursday. Honestly I'm the nervous one ❤️
First day of first grade. Kwame came out of Greenlawn this afternoon and told me his teacher is "nice but strict," which sounds about right.
Curriculum Night at Greenlawn. First grade is reading, writing, and the class fish Kwame campaigned to name Sparky.

Blown fuse? Replace it with the exact same rating and type. If it called for slow-blow, it gets slow-blow. A bigger fuse doesn't solve anything, it just lets the real fault cook something that costs a lot more than a fuse.
Reggie at Fresh Edge fixed what the summer did to my hairline. Twenty minutes in the chair and an hour of Pistons opinions.
Church this morning, then jollof at Auntie Abena's. Kwame is on his third plate and I'm not far behind him.
heads up, it's dark by 7:45 now. front AND rear lights or you're not rolling

Pioneer SX-780 is back from the bench and ready for a new home. Power supply recapped, new dial lamps, every function checked against spec. We grade it Very Good, and the full photo set and bench report are on our Instagram shop. Local pick-up in Bagley or shipped UPS Ground, message us with questions.

Same bench, new colors. Our look is now VU Amber, the glow of a meter on a receiver that's been warming up for ten minutes. We've also moved to corktownaudio.com, so update your bookmarks. Inventory, our grading guide and how to reach us are all there.
Love the new look over at Corktown Audio Works. That amber is exactly the color of a meter when the needle drops. Avenue of Fashion folks, go check out corktownaudio.com.

Ten years ago this fall I was swapping instrument clusters in Dearborn. Today I spent the afternoon packing receivers with Ama, and she called my box job "acceptable." High praise from the shipping department.
Block club meets Tuesday at 7pm at Lorraine Pettiford's on Prairie. Agenda: snow shoveling list for our seniors, the vacant lot on the corner, and Halloween plans. Coffee and pound cake provided!
Block club at Lorraine's tonight. Signed up for the snow shoveling list again. Somebody has to keep Doris and Earl's walk clear, and Kwame loves the shovel more than the sled.

Spot the difference: a cold solder joint looks dull and grainy, sometimes with a ring around the lead. A good one is smooth and shiny. When we find a cold joint we clean it, add fresh solder and reflow, because old solder on its own won't flow right.
Ride's at 6:00 tonight. Roosevelt Park as usual. Usual loop, about 25 miles, and lights are not optional.
Cold one at Rollers tonight. Full gloves came out for the first time. Darnell showed up in shorts like it's July.

No-tools speed check for your turntable: print a strobe disc, set it on the platter, and light it with an incandescent bulb, which flickers at 60 Hz here. If the dots drift, your speed is off. Most cheap LEDs won't work for this because they don't flicker the same way.
Coming soon to the shop: a silver Technics SL-1200MK2, freshly serviced and locked on the strobe at 33 and 45. Full photos and the grade are on the way. Questions are welcome in the meantime.
Halloween is a week from today. The robot costume passed its last fitting, lights and all, and Kwame now answers questions in beeps.
